question: How does a fan-out mode cut change the declared coverage and single-worker fragility of Demerzel's worker-to-work-class graph?
production_path: investigation: inspect pinned Demerzel worker-lane policy and advisory selector
graph: worker to assigned role to work class with mode-filtered paths
metric: covered assigned classes and classes with at least two worker neighbors
counterfactual: delete one worker vertex in DRAINING
experiment: predict selector replay outcomes from the pinned graph
hypothesis: A mode-filtered worker-class graph can identify declared routing coverage and fragile single-worker classes, provided its edges are not mistaken for worker availability, exact-role equivalence, or permission to act.
evidence: At Demerzel commit ecdc6c27559bb1a11343cfad33687465893e9891, state/driver/aiw-worker-lanes.json declares five workers and primary, secondary, and forbidden role lists, with each named role mapped to a work class and four fan-out mode block lists. The file calls the selector advisory and dry-run.

A read-only calculation over the pinned JSON found 22 primary-or-secondary worker-role assignments. Five work classes occur in those assignments. After mapping and deduplicating worker-class pairs, NORMAL has 9 edges with class degrees fix 2, groom 2, navigate 1, net_new_feature 1, review 3.

Filtering the pinned mode_blocks gives 8 worker-class edges and 4/5 class coverage in CONSTRAINED and DRAINING, and 3 edges and 1/5 coverage in HALTED. In DRAINING, removing augment eliminates navigate and reduces coverage to 3/5; removing any other single worker loses no whole class.

At the same commit, scripts/aiw_lane_selector.py checks forbidden role membership before assigned-role membership, blocks mode-filtered classes, yields allow for an unblocked primary role and recommend for an unblocked secondary role, and says exit code 0 means evaluated rather than allowed.

The offline replay was run on 2026-10-12 after checking the policy and selector Git blobs against pinned commit ecdc6c27559bb1a11343cfad33687465893e9891. It observed 22, 21, 21, and 8 unblocked assigned-role paths across NORMAL, CONSTRAINED, DRAINING, and HALTED; projected worker-class edges were 9, 8, 8, and 3; unblocked primary paths were 5, 4, 4, and 1. Forbidden, unknown-role, and unknown-mode controls returned block, warn, and escalate. The deterministic JSON receipt is state/streeling/reviews/net-003-selector-replay-2026-10-12.json. No live worker, authorization, task completion, learner attempt, or publication was verified. Research duration was not instrumented, so duration_seconds=0.
